object_description: staged sports-campus ensemble with a gateway building
design_condition: The first-stage building marks the town entrance and urban edge, while the route network, green buffer, car parks, and sports fields organize the site around the existing topography with minimal earth movement.

positive.statement: The project develops a clear and coherent urban plan involving the entire area.
The first-stage building acts as an important entrance sign and clearly delimits the urbanized area from the agricultural area.
The route network defines external spaces with clear functions and responds to the topography without major earth movements.
The arrangement of green areas, buildings, and car parks convincingly highlights the void formed by the correctly oriented football fields.
The park creates a buffer and incorporates a large biotope for managing rainwater.
The direct connection to the route creates a qualitative and easily identifiable entrance space.
Compositional and constructional simplicity gives the building architectural quality.
The multi-purpose room benefits from the portico and can support the gyms.
The prefabricated concrete construction follows the cost-containment objective.

negative.statement: The parking layout during the first stage raises doubts before the project is fully executed.
The dividing glass parts require further study of both acoustic and visual aspects.
The basement service-space organization is criticized from the standpoint of sports functionality.
